suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-7 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Physiologically relevant hiatal hernia as an anatomic contributor to objectively established gastroesophageal reflux disease. Require a documented hiatal hernia, with the source proposition most directly applicable to a sliding or otherwise physiologically relevant gastroesophageal-junction hernia, and a separately established diagnosis of GERD using appropriate clinical, endoscopic, or reflux-monitoring evidence. Do not infer GERD solely from the presence of a hiatal hernia. Preserve lower-esophageal-sphincter dysfunction, obesity, medications, delayed gastric emptying, dietary or behavioral contributors, prior foregut surgery, and other reflux causes. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
